approved: Freedom of Information Amendment (New Arrangements) Bill 2014

Moved the Freedom of Information Amendment (New Arrangements) Bill, which abolishes the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner and gives the Administrative Appeals Tribunal sole responsibility for external merits review of FOI decisions, saving $10.2 million over four years.

Argued against the Freedom of Information Amendment (New Arrangements) Bill for abolishing the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, and separately condemned the government for failing to publish a Women's Budget Statement for the first time in 30 years, since 1984.

Opposed changes abolishing the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, arguing that freedom of information promotes transparency and accountability, that the new review system had operated as intended, and that returning review functions to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal would make access harder for the public.

Argued that government should favour openness in freedom of information, criticised withholding information about Operation Sovereign Borders and EastWest Link cost-benefit analyses, and opposed abolishing independent oversight through the Freedom of Information Amendment (New Arrangements) Bill.

Announced that the Freedom of Information Amendment (New Arrangements) Bill will streamline privacy and freedom of information functions from 1 January 2015, while preserving access rights, removing one layer of external merits review, and addressing duplication and delays.
